column1: # The package set, and the single source of truth for it.
# BuildNugets.sh packs in this order, the release and PR workflows generate their package tables
# from it, and run-emulator-tests.sh clears the local NuGet cache for every id listed here. Adding
# a package means adding a row here and a project under src/ - nothing else has a second copy of
# the list to fall out of step with.
# Rows are in dependency order: a package's dd-deps must already have appeared above it.
# name                   maven-artifact-id                        dd-deps (this repo's package names, or -)

# NOT BOUND, and why.
# Datadog publishes 41 dd-sdk-android* artifacts on Maven Central (counted 2026-07 against the
# https://repo1.maven.org/maven2/com/datadoghq/ index); the 13 above are the ones a .NET or MAUI
# app can use today. This section exists so "is X missing on purpose?" has an answer here rather
# than in someone's memory - and it doubles as the machine-read roster: the upstream-watch
# workflow greps the dd-sdk-android* ids out of this whole file and opens an issue when Central
# grows an artifact that is neither bound above nor listed below. Keep every entry a FULL
# artifact id for that reason.
#   dd-sdk-android                            An umbrella/BOM artifact, not a library.
#   dd-sdk-android-gradle-plugin              A Gradle build plugin. Nothing to bind.
#   dd-sdk-android-gradle-plugin-kcp-common   Gradle build-time tooling: the plugin's Kotlin
#   dd-sdk-android-gradle-plugin-kcp-kotlin20 compiler-plugin variants, one per Kotlin version.
#   dd-sdk-android-gradle-plugin-kcp-kotlin21 Not bindable - none of it ships in an app.
#   dd-sdk-android-gradle-plugin-kcp-kotlin22
#   dd-sdk-android-gradle-plugin-kcp-kotlin24
#   dd-sdk-android-benchmark-internal         Datadog's own benchmarking harness, not product API.
#   dd-sdk-android-ktx                        Kotlin extension functions. They bind as static
#   dd-sdk-android-rx                         methods on synthetic *Kt classes taking Kotlin
#   dd-sdk-android-rum-coroutines             function interfaces, and every one of them wraps a
#   dd-sdk-android-trace-coroutines           Kotlin idiom - coroutines, Rx, scope functions -
#                                             that has no C# meaning. A caller would write more
#                                             code than they saved.
#   dd-sdk-android-coil                       Instrument third-party Kotlin/Java libraries -
#   dd-sdk-android-coil3                      image loaders, an HTTP stack, a GraphQL client, a
#   dd-sdk-android-fresco                     database layer, a logger. A MAUI app draws through
#   dd-sdk-android-glide                      MAUI handlers, loads images through MAUI and speaks
#   dd-sdk-android-sqldelight                 HTTP through the BCL or OkHttp, so none of these
#   dd-sdk-android-timber                     libraries is present to instrument. Add the
#   dd-sdk-android-cronet                     artifact yourself if you host native code that
#   dd-sdk-android-apollo                     uses one.
#   dd-sdk-android-rum-debug-widget           An in-app Compose overlay for debugging RUM
#                                             instrumentation from the device. Developer tooling
#                                             for Compose apps, not meaningful in MAUI.
#   dd-sdk-android-compose                    RUM auto-instrumentation for Jetpack Compose -
#                                             distinct from session-replay-compose, which IS
#                                             bound. Nothing in MAUI draws Compose. Worth
#                                             revisiting for an app hosting Compose content.
#   dd-sdk-android-tv                         Android TV. Worth revisiting if .NET for Android
#                                             TV becomes a target.
#   dd-sdk-android-trace-otel                 OpenTelemetry interop. Reachable in principle, but
#   dd-sdk-android-okhttp-otel                a .NET app that wants OTel semantics is better
#                                             served by the OpenTelemetry .NET SDK exporting to
#                                             Datadog's OTLP intake than by a binding over Java's.
#   dd-sdk-android-flags                      Binding candidates, not yet bound: feature-flag
#   dd-sdk-android-flags-openfeature          evaluation (plus its OpenFeature provider) and the
#   dd-sdk-android-profiling                  profiler are new enough that no consumer has asked;
#                                             file an issue if you need one and it moves up.
